Totally agree. After further investigation I've realized that the `_prefix` option is not implemented. I will work on that. 

`cache_dir` and `timeout` are properly implemented but not prefix:

```python
            self._cache_dir = self._get_cache_connection(self.get_option('_uri'))
            self._timeout = float(self.get_option('_timeout'))
```
I will implement and test it ASAP

preifx option was for caches that used an RDBMS to prefix table names, none of the file based plugins implement it

but easy to fix that
```
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/cache/__init__.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/cache/__init__.py
index 3b337835d0..08c4f5c73d 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/cache/__init__.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/cache/__init__.py
@@ -147,7 +147,12 @@ class BaseFileCacheModule(BaseCacheModule):
             if self.has_expired(key) or key == "":
                 raise KeyError

-            cachefile = "%s/%s" % (self._cache_dir, key)
+            prefix = self.get_option('_prefix')
+            if prefix:
+                cachefile = "%s/%s_%s" % (self._cache_dir, prefix, key)
+            else:
+                cachefile = "%s/%s" % (self._cache_dir, key)
+
             try:
                 value = self._load(cachefile)
                 self._cache[key] = value
```

It seems no one really uses the feature though, its been this way for a long time, it took a while to be noticed ....
